title: Space to Ground: On a Roll: June 16, 2023
description: NASA's Space to Ground is your weekly update on what's happening aboard the International Space Station.

transcript.text: WELCOME TO SPACE TO GROUND.
I AM KAYLA LaFRANCE.
ITS BEEN A MARATHON OF SPACEWALKS THIS MONTH AS THE CREW ABOARD
THE INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION CONTINUES TO
IMPROVE AND UPDATE THE ORBITING LABORATORY.
LAST FRIDAY, NASA ASTRONAUTS AND EXPEDITION 69 CREW MEMBERS
STEVE BOWEN AND WOODY HOBURG CONCLUDED THEIR FIRST OF TWO
SPACEWALKS AFTER 6 HOURS AND 3 MINUTES OUTSIDE THE SPACE STATION.
BOWEN AND HOBURG COMPLETED ALL OF THE OBJECTIVES
FOR THE FIRST SPACEWALK TO INSTALL AN IROSA
TO AUGMENT POWER GENERATION FOR THE 1A POWER CHANNEL
ON THE STATION’S STARBOARD TRUSS STRUCTURE.
THE DYNAMIC DUO VENTURED BACK OUTSIDE ON THURSDAY THIS WEEK
TO INSTALL THE SIXTH IN THE SERIES OF IROSAS
ON THE STARBOARD 6 TRUSS OF THE STATION FOR THE 1B POWER CHANNEL.
THIS WEEK’S SPACEWALK WAS THE 265TH SPACEWALK IN SUPPORT OF
SPACE STATION ASSEMBLY, UPGRADES, AND MAINTENANCE.
IT WAS THE TENTH SPACEWALK FOR BOWEN, AND THE SECOND FOR HOBURG.
AND JOIN US NEXT WEEK WHEN ROSCOSMOS COSMONAUTS
DON THEIR ORLAN SPACE SUITES AND VENTURE OUTSIDE
TO REMOVE EXPERIMENT HARDWARE AND INSTALL
NEW DATA TRANSMISSION HARDWARE.
THIS SPACEWALK WILL TAKE PLACE
ON THURSDAY, JUNE 22ND AT APPROX. 10:20 A.M. EASTERN
AND IS SCHEDULED TO LAST ABOUT SEVEN HOURS.
THE INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION
IS A GLOBAL OBSERVATION AND DIAGNOSIS STATION.
IT PROMOTES INTERNATIONAL EARTH OBSERVATIONS
AIMED AT UNDERSTANDING AND RESOLVING
THE ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES OF OUR HOME PLANET.
THE SPACE STATION OFFERS A UNIQUE VANTAGE POINT
FOR OBSERVING THE EARTH'S ECOSYSTEMS
WITH HANDS-ON AND AUTOMATED EQUIPMENT.
THESE OPTIONS ENABLE ASTRONAUTS TO OBSERVE
AND EXPLAIN WHAT THEY WITNESS IN REAL TIME.
IN RECENT WEEKS, THE CREW OF THE SPACE STATION
HAVE BEEN PHOTOGRAPHING THE WILDFIRES CURRENTLY BURNING ACROSS CANADA.
THESE PHOTOS OF THE FIRE NEAR SHELBURNE NOVA SCOTIA,
WERE TAKEN ON MAY 29.
WITHIN A FEW DAYS,
THE FIRE HAD SCORCHED OVER 75 SQUARE MILES,
MAKING IT THE LARGEST FOREST FIRE IN NOVA SCOTIA'S HISTORY.
THE SMOKE FROM THESE WILDFIRE CAUSED HISTORICALLY POOR AIR QUALITY
IN THE NORTHEASTERN REGION OF THE UNITED STATES.
YOU CAN ALSO BROWSE AND DOWNLOAD IMAGERY OF SATELLITE DATA
FROM NASA’S CONSTELLATION OF EARTH OBSERVING SATELLITES.
HEAD OVER TO EARTHOBSERVATORY.NASA.GOV AND EXPLORE OUR WORLD FROM ABOVE.
THAT’S SPACE TO GROUND FOR THIS WEEK.
THANKS FOR WATCHING.
WE’LL SEE YOU NEXT WEEK.
